exact_items: FileManager.md universalizes OpenFile to cover all object-open semantics, including identity-native subject opens that belong to a different contract family
FileManager.md must be narrowed to workspace-document path operations only; the OpenSubject family belongs in a separate contract
notes: FileManager.md OpenFile overclaim confirmed again in GPT-5.3-Codex synthesis. Must narrow to workspace path operations; identity-native/subject-open family is a separate contract.

exact_items: Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md shows artifacts but provides no documented linkage from usage receipts to runtime artifacts
The receipt→artifact join is the critical projection step that populates the panel; without a documented linkage, implementations will diverge
notes: Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md must document the receipt→artifact linkage model: which fields join, which event triggers panel population, and which contract owns the join specification

exact_items: Contracts_V0.md has no route-target contract — the canonical shape that all navigation/subject-open commands and surface pivots must conform to
Add a concrete route_target contract to Contracts_V0.md with minimum required fields and a normalization rule for surface-specific IDs
notes: Contracts_V0.md needs a canonical route_target contract shape. This is the foundational contract for all navigation/pivot/subject-open operations across the app.

exact_items: resume_url is currently positioned as a canonical route-target contract field, but its semantics are transport-layer (serialized URL) not application-layer (structured route model)
resume_url must be demoted to a transport-only serialized form; the canonical route model must be the structured route_target contract
notes: resume_url is an architecture inversion: it treats serialized URL as the canonical model rather than as a serialized transport of a structured route_target. The contract must explicitly demote resume_url to transport-only.

exact_items: Project_Output_Artifacts.md draft lineage is described in a subject-first model but there is no link from the draft lineage to a route-target contract
Connect the draft lineage model to the route-target contract so draft artifacts can be opened, referenced, and routed through the canonical navigation model
notes: Project_Output_Artifacts.md draft lineage is subject-first but unlinked to the route-target contract. This gap means draft artifacts cannot be routed through the canonical navigation model.

exact_items: workflow_run_id vs run_id lineage conflict in Project_Output_Artifacts.md is confirmed again in the GPT-5.3-Codex synthesis
This is a blocking naming conflict that must be resolved before any automated tooling can safely emit or consume these records
notes: GPT-5.3-Codex synthesis confirms workflow_run_id/run_id conflict. run_id is the canonical form (aligned with attempt_id/run/storage conventions); workflow_run_id should be tombstoned.

exact_items: run-gates script has no numbered gate mapping — it cannot associate a gate label (GATE-001 through GATE-015) with an executable check
The gate registry in Progression_Gates.md must export a machine-readable numbered mapping that run-gates can import
notes: Progression_Gates.md gate registry must export (or reference) a numbered machine-readable mapping for the run-gates pipeline script. Without it, gates can't be associated with executable checks.

exact_items: pm.evidence.schema.v1 binary pass/fail gap is confirmed a third time in GPT-5.3-Codex synthesis
The tri-state extension (pass/fail/skipped) to pm.evidence.schema.v1 is a blocking deficiency for multiple gates
notes: Third independent finding: pm.evidence.schema.v1 binary verdicts are blocking. Tri-state extension is required before gate verification tooling can be built. Priority: high.
